FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, October 15, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: Staff will follow up with AVP Lavan about sharing the Academic Program Review Handbook/Manual that his office is developing.
FSEC awaits reviews by CBUM regarding proposed legislation and comments from TAAC regarding required syllabus statements.
Liaisons are asked to monitor progress and ensure written responses are provided.
Sen.
Trimm will provide the draft statement on campus police as relates to ICE to the SCLC so they might make recommendations.
Staff will invite the VP RED to an FSEC meeting soon to discuss “required training mandates” and myriad other research-related interests.
Sen.
Trimm will continue fact-finding related to policies that would apply to recording classroom activities and otherwise preventing disruptive behavior (politically motivated or otherwise) in the classroom. 1.
Call to Order - FS President Williams called the meeting to order at 10:01.
VP Preisser and Sens.
Daniels, Trimm and Van Wyk were present, along with ex officio member Ted Walls. 2.

Minutes for approval - Minutes of the 10/8/25 meeting.
The minutes were approved as edited. 3.
Guests: Christopher Lavan, Assoc.
Vice Provost for Advancement of Teaching and Learning, and Assoc.
Professor of Education Shane Tutwiler, Chair, Joint Committee for Academic Program Review and Outcomes Assessment (JAPROA) joined the meeting.
AVP Lavan started off by outlining the work of the ATL office, noting that it supports the work of committees like JAPROA and JCODL in an advisory and consultative way.
Some history and background was provided on the work of prior iterations of these committees and by former key staffers in the ATL office.
AVP Lavan and Chair Tutwiler stressed that the faculty-led committees retain the authority to conduct reviews within well-established processes, but the scope of that authority seems to confuse some faculty members.
It was noted that JAPROA is a newer committee that only experienced its first full operational year in AY24-25.

Committee members too struggled with the line between “advising” and “approving.” In short, when an undergraduate program is proposed by a department or college, the outcomes assessment portion of that proposal is assigned to JAPROA, which undertakes its work with assistance from the ATL office.
Also, the office has been developing a “Manual” or handbook that outlines the academic program review process which should become a valuable resource for departments undergoing reviews.
Chair Tutwiler noted that the guidance is drawn from Chapter 8 of the University Manual and the committee is keenly interested in simplifying the process to make it easier for departments to undertake.
He considers the work of his committee to be invaluable in guiding metaprocesses and ensuring that the university, through all aggregated academic units, continues to learn from self-study and reflection, and therefore improves and succeeds.
While JAPROA’s role involves providing feedback on outcomes assessments, they can only adopt and forward recommendations, but the final decisions always rest in the departments.

Wrapping up, FSEC members suggested that the draft manual be shared with the membership, and the committees might consider a graphic presentation of their workflows and processes which might enhance understanding. 4.
Priority Items 4.1 Green Hall Meeting Prep (10/29) - Several potential agenda items were discussed for the joint meeting between the FSEC and the university President, Provost and Vice Provost.
These ranged from the Federal Department of Education’s higher education “Compact,” to 1

department-level system administrator permissions from IT services.
The final list of talking points will be determined next week. 4.2 Meeting Prep October 16 Senate meeting - The Committee revisited the initiatives being formally introduced this month and discussed presentations.
There are some unknowns in that it is difficult to predict how long some presentations will run.
Standing committee chairs have been asked to be brief and it is hoped the annual photograph can be accomplished expeditiously. 4.3 Set weekly meeting schedule for spring semester - As not everyone continues to be available on Wednesday mornings next semester, staff will administer an availability poll asap. 5.
Continued Items 5.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - Two newly submitted concerns were addressed, one of which was a reiteration of previous submission. 5.2 Committee Assignment Updates - Finalize Joint Committees - Several candidates have been contacted and responses should be forthcoming.
Most open seats are ready for appointments on 10/16. 5.3 Elimination of Budget Statement Requirement - Tabled to next week. 5.4 Graduate School external report - Pres.

Williams has mentioned the report to the Vice Provost in hopes of learning more about the administration’s reaction to it.
The Full FSEC will plan to discuss the content at their joint 10/29 meeting with administrators. 5.5 Centers and Institutes Discussion - continued discussion, esp. revisions to UM Sec. 8.90.20 - The CIRC has the draft proposal and is reviewing it.
Pres.
Williams is meeting with the Provost and Vice Provost about the specific proposal on 10/24. 6.
Updates 6.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) i.
APC Meeting 10/14/25 - Pres.
Williams explained that he had voted against the tuition policy as presented, but approval was granted by the APC and it will now go to the BOT for adoption.
Current BOT members, relative to governance under the Board of Education, while having espoused a commitment to accessibility, seem distanced from RI voters and taxpayers in a way that might put them out of touch with the average student and their demographics and means.
Other positions expressed by Pres.

Williams included concerns about the role of market forces in determining tuition, fees, and charges and the real versus perceived transparency of approval procedures for changes to tuition, fees, and charges.
All members of APC were willing to have the deep conversations necessary to effect a comprehensive reorientation of the tuition policy, but everyone, including Pres.
Williams, recognized that there was insufficient time available for such conversations to affect the current draft language, which needs to be approved before the end of the calendar year, and that the mooted policy was better than no policy at all.
It is unknown as yet if the student and faculty representatives to the BOT will make comments during the review and adoption process.
